thread:
Aliza: Quick sync — API contract question about the generation endpoint. Two related items: (1) precedence/semantics when both termination sequences and max_tokens are provided, and (2) how logprobs are reported when a stop causes truncation. Also pushed a tiny test to cover a related edgecase (PR #342). PTAL @Mike @Sasha

Aliza: Example request for context:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-1",
  "prompt": "Translate: Hello",
  "max_tokens": 100,
  "stop": ["\n--END--"],
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```

Mike: Short answer: stop sequences take precedence — we stop emitting once a stop sequence is emitted, even if max_tokens not reached. max_tokens remains a hard cap. However, we currently have ambiguity about whether the stop token is included in the returned text and whether it's present in the logprobs arrays. Runtime behavior: we strip stop text from returned "text" but still include the matching token(s) in the token stream and logprobs. That mismatch needs to be spelled out in the contract.

Sasha: +1. Also flagging temp/top_p behavior: when temperature==0 we do greedy decoding. We need to explicitly document whether top_p is honored in that codepath. I recommend a deterministic rule: if temp==0 => ignore top_p and sample_mode=greedy. Add a unit test for temp=0 + top_p=0.5.

Jordan: We should surface this in docs and call it out in release notes — some customers rely on deterministic outputs for safety pipelines.

Mike: Edge cases to test: overlapping stop sequences (e.g., ["abc", "bc"]). We also need to decide how partial matches across chunk boundaries are handled (the runtime only matches on emitted text boundaries right now). Add an integration test where stop sequence straddles the kv cache chunk.

Aliza: For logprobs specifically: do we include the token that matched the stop in the logprobs array? Current behavior includes it. Question: should we instead omit it to make text/logprobs align more obviously? Thoughts?

Kevin: Perf note — computing logprobs is nontrivial on quantized kernels, it adds ~10-20% latency on our internal benchmarks. We should add a cost multiplier for logprobs in the Console and warn customers. Also consider lazy computation (only for top-k requested).

Deploybot: Deploybot: canary rollout for gen-runtime v2.4 started at 1891234580; watch /metrics/gen/stop_match_rate and /metrics/latency/p95 for canary nodes.

Mike: Also code-review ping: PTAL @Mike on PRs #342 (test) and #348 (stop matching fixes). If we agree on contract language I can land the runtime change.

Aliza: Action items:
- Aliza -> open spec PR that documents: stop precedence, whether stop tokens are included in returned text, exact logprobs semantics, finish_reason values.
- Mike -> confirm token inclusion semantics and add unit/integration tests.
- Sasha -> add deterministic note for temp==0 behavior + tests.
- Kevin -> provide perf delta and a suggested cost multiplier to show in Console.

Aliza: I'll update this thread with PR links. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
